label: model_selection_iter2
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Swap the ranking generator: replace hist_gbdt with xgboost, a different GBDT implementation with row<path> subsampling and stronger L2, using many shallow trees instead of 400 deep-ish histogram trees. Fit on all 2,760 training rows (no early stopping, so no rows are given up to an internal stopping slice), keep the default decision rule and no class weighting, and keep preprocessing identical to iteration 1 (median impute — a no-op here since there is no missingness — and no scaling, since trees are scale-invariant). Concretely: xgboost with n_estimators=900, learning_rate=0.03, max_depth=5, min_child_weight=3, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.7, reg_lambda=2.0, reg_alpha=0.5. Then read roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut and cut_headroom again: if the ranking (KS) rises materially toward the required 0.934, push the same family harder next; if it lands within noise of hist_gbdt's 0.9789 roc_auc, the two GBDT implementations share a ceiling on this file and the next attempt goes to a structurally different ranking generator (extra_trees or svc with an RBF kernel on scaled columns).",
  "model_family": "gbdt",
  "candidate_models": [
    "xgboost",
    "extra_trees",
    "svc"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 900,
    "learning_rate": 0.03,
    "max_depth": 5,
    "min_child_weight": 3,
    "subsample": 0.8,
    "colsample_bytree": 0.7,
    "reg_lambda": 2.0,
    "reg_alpha": 0.5
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Different estimator family<path>: xgboost instead of hist_gbdt. Capacity is redistributed rather than increased — 900 rounds at learning_rate 0.03 with depth capped at 5 (vs 400 rounds at 0.06 with 31 leaves), plus regularisers hist_gbdt did not have: subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.7, min_child_weight 3, reg_lambda 2.0, reg_alpha 0.5. Operating point and preprocessing are deliberately unchanged (no class_weight / scale_pos_weight, median impute, no scaling), and early stopping stays off so all 2,760 training rows are fitted, keeping the score directly comparable to iteration 1.",
  "rationale": "The Critic's verdict is wrong_model_family and the arithmetic supports it: cut_headroom is 0.008074, so every operating-point lever combined can close at most ~22% of the 0.0368 shortfall — class_weight is not the lever, and recall 0.9088 vs specificity 0.9516 confirms the cut is already near-optimal. Capacity of the current family is also exhausted: train_balanced_accuracy 0.9991 with train_val_gap 0.0688 means the ensemble already memorises the training split, so more iterations or leaves of the same generator cannot raise the ranking. The only remaining axis is the ranking itself, and with just one family measured the family-swap span on this file is unknown. xgboost is the cheapest structurally different ranking generator available: it is a different split-finding and regularisation scheme, and its row+column subsampling produces a genuinely different (less memorising, better-averaged) ranking rather than another point in hist_gbdt's hyperparameter space. Depth 5 with min_child_weight 3 and colsample 0.7 attacks the over-flexibility the Critic flagged, while 900 rounds at lr 0.03 preserves total fitting power. Runtime is a non-issue (iteration 1 took 4.7 s of 600 s; ~900 depth-5 trees on 2,760 rows × 57 features stays well inside both the time and 2,048 MB budgets). Note the honest expectation: recorded family swaps have moved roc_auc by 0.0022–0.0077, while the bar needs the ranking (KS) to rise 0.0874 from the baseline — 0.0574 above this model's KS 0.8766 — so one swap may not clear 0.967. This attempt is priced as the measurement that tells us whether the ranking axis has room on this file at all, and it explicitly sets up a non-GBDT generator (extra_trees, or svc with RBF on standardised columns) for the next iteration if the two GBDT implementations agree.",
  "unsupported_claims": [],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 2
}
